title: Most Candy Kinds
description: `candies[i]` is the kind of the `i`-th candy; the length is even. You may eat exactly half of the candies. Return the largest number of different kinds you can eat.

examples.explanation: You can taste at most 3 kind(s).
You can taste at most 2 kind(s).

title: Maximum Units On Truck
description: `boxes` holds pairs `[count0, units0, count1, units1, ...]`: there are `count` boxes of a type and each box holds `units` units. A truck can carry at most `truckSize` boxes. Return the maximum total number of units the truck can carry.

title: Fewest Clock Steps
description: `current` and `correct` are times written `HH:MM` on a 24-hour clock, with `correct` the same as or later than `current` on the same day. In one step you may add `1`, `5`, `15` or `60` minutes to the current time. Return the minimum number of steps to reach `correct`.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of steps is 3.
The minimum number of steps is 1.

constraints: both strings match HH:MM with 00 <= HH <= 23 and 00 <= MM <= 59

title: Minimum Four-Digit Split Sum
description: Split the four digits of `num` (a four-digit number) into two two-digit numbers `a` and `b` using every digit exactly once; leading zeros are allowed. Return the minimum possible value of `a + b`.
constraints: every digit must be used exactly once

title: Bottles Drunk With Exchange
description: You start with `numBottles` full bottles. After drinking you may exchange `numExchange` empty bottles for one full bottle; every time you do this, `numExchange` increases by `1`. Return the largest number of bottles you can drink.

title: Pizza Slices Share
description: There are `3n` pizza slices with sizes in `slices`. Repeatedly you pick any three slices: your friend takes the largest of the three, you take the second largest and the last friend takes the smallest. Return the maximum total size you can collect after all slices are taken.
constraints: 3 <= slices.length <= 10^5 and slices.length is a multiple of 3

title: Cheapest Chip Alignment
description: Chips sit at the positions in `position`. Moving a chip by `2` costs nothing; moving a chip by `1` costs `1`. Return the minimum total cost to bring all chips to one common position.

title: Hidden Number Guess Count
description: A secret number lies in `1..n`. You guess by binary search: with the current range `[lo, hi]` you guess `mid = (lo + hi) / 2` rounded down, and if it is too low you set `lo = mid + 1`, if too high you set `hi = mid - 1`. Return how many guesses are needed to hit `secret`.

examples.explanation: The secret is found after 3 guess(es).
The secret is found after 1 guess(es).

title: First Failing Build
description: `results` is sorted: all passing builds (`0`) come before all failing builds (`1`). Return the index of the first failing build, or `-1` if every build passes.

examples.explanation: The first failing build is at index 2 (-1 means none).
The first failing build is at index -1 (-1 means none).

constraints: results[i] is 0 or 1 and the array is non-decreasing

title: Minimum Time Visiting All Points
description: `points` holds pairs `[x0, y0, x1, y1, ...]`. In one second you can move one unit horizontally, vertically or diagonally (changing both coordinates by one). Return the minimum number of seconds to visit all points in the given order.

examples.explanation: The minimum travel time is 7 seconds.
The minimum travel time is 5 seconds.

title: Positive Versus Negative Count
description: `nums` is sorted in non-decreasing order. Return the larger of two counts: the number of negative values and the number of positive values (zeros belong to neither).

title: Running Kth Largest Total
description: Numbers from `nums` arrive one at a time. After every arrival that leaves at least `k` numbers received, take the `k`-th largest number received so far (duplicates counted separately). Return the sum of these values.

examples.explanation: The running k-th largest values add up to 12.
The running k-th largest values add up to 6.

title: Sum Of K Most Frequent Values
description: Rank the distinct values of `nums` by how often they occur (more occurrences first); values with equal frequency are ranked with the smaller value first. Return the sum of the first `k` values in this ranking.

examples.explanation: The top-k values add up to 3.
The top-k values add up to 11.

constraints: -10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4, 1 <= k <= number of distinct values

title: Rounds To Zero By Smallest Subtraction
description: In one round you take the smallest positive value `x` in `nums` and subtract `x` from every positive element. Return the number of rounds needed to make every element equal to `0`.

title: Fewest Rounds To Fill Cups
description: There are `a`, `b` and `c` cups of three kinds of water to fill. In one round you may fill two cups of different kinds, or one cup of any kind. Return the minimum number of rounds to fill all cups.

title: Candy Shop Free Third
description: A shop gives a free candy for every two candies you buy: after choosing two candies you may take a third for free, but its price must be at most the cheaper of the two bought. Return the minimum total cost to take all candies in `prices`.

title: Steps To Reach Zero
description: Starting from `num`, each step divides it by `2` if it is even, otherwise subtracts `1`. Return the number of steps needed to reach `0`.

title: Ways With Two Coin Types
description: Return the number of pairs of non-negative integers `(x, y)` such that `a * x + b * y == n`.

title: Divisor Game Winner
description: Two players alternate, Alice first, with a number `n` on the board. A move picks `x` with `0 < x < n` and `n % x == 0` and replaces `n` by `n - x`. A player who cannot move loses. Return `true` if Alice wins with optimal play.

title: Remaining Stones After Halving
description: Perform the following exactly `k` times: take the largest pile in `piles` and remove `floor(x / 2)` stones from it, where `x` is its size. Return the total number of stones left.

title: Integer Cube Root Floor
description: Return the largest integer `r` such that `r * r * r <= x`.

examples.explanation: The floor of the cube root is 3.
The floor of the cube root is 2.

constraints: do not use built-in power or root functions

title: Count In Range Sorted
description: `nums` is sorted in non-decreasing order. Return how many elements `v` satisfy `lo <= v <= hi`.
constraints: -10^9 <= nums[i], lo, hi <= 10^9, nums is sorted and lo <= hi

title: Money Left After Two Items
description: Buy exactly two items from `prices` so that their total cost is as small as possible. If the two cheapest items together cost at most `money`, return the money left after buying them; otherwise buy nothing and return `money`.

title: Profit With Repeated Round Trips
description: `prices[i]` is a stock's price on day `i`. You may buy and sell as many times as you like, but you can hold at most one share at a time. Return the maximum total profit.

title: Moves With Doubles
description: You start at `1` and want to reach `target`. In one move you may add `1`, or double the number (at most `maxDoubles` times in total). Return the minimum number of moves.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of moves is 7.
The minimum number of moves is 4.

title: Product Of Two Minus One
description: Choose two different indices `i` and `j` of `nums`. Return the maximum value of `(nums[i] - 1) * (nums[j] - 1)`.

title: Closest Neighbour Pair Count
description: `nums` has distinct values. Sort it and look at neighbouring values. Return how many neighbouring pairs have the smallest difference found among all neighbouring pairs.

examples.explanation: 3 neighbouring pair(s) share the smallest gap.
1 neighbouring pair(s) share the smallest gap.

title: Tasks Done Within Time
description: Task `i` takes `tasks[i]` minutes and tasks can be done in any order, one after another. Return the largest number of tasks that can be completed within `T` minutes in total.

title: Dominoes On Two-By-N Board
description: Count the ways to tile a board with `2` rows and `n` columns using `1 x 2` dominoes (each placed horizontally or vertically) with no gaps and no overlaps.
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer

title: Fence Colouring Ways
description: A fence has `n` posts and you have `k` colours. Paint every post so that no three consecutive posts share the same colour. Return the number of ways to paint the fence.
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer

title: Fewest Powers Of Two
description: Return the minimum number of powers of two (`1, 2, 4, 8, ...`, repetition allowed) whose sum is exactly `n`.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of powers is 4.
The minimum number of powers is 1.

constraints: each term must be a power of two

title: Repeated Min Multiplication Sum
description: Perform `k` operations on `nums`: find the minimum value (the leftmost one on ties) and multiply it by `m`. Return the sum of all elements after the operations, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: The sum after all operations is 29.
The sum after all operations is 24.

title: Kth Divisible By Either
description: Return the `k`-th smallest positive integer that is divisible by `a` or by `b` (or both).

title: Wiggle Possible Check
description: Return `true` if the elements of `nums` can be rearranged so that no two neighbouring elements are equal.

title: Watering Walk Steps
description: Plant `i` stands at position `i` (positions `0..n-1`) and needs `plants[i]` units of water; the river is at position `-1`. You walk left to right with a can of capacity `capacity` (filled at the start), watering each plant fully. If the water is not enough for the next plant you walk back to the river, refill and walk back. Return the number of steps walked. Every plant needs at most `capacity` units.

title: Best Rod Cutting Revenue
description: A rod of length `L` can be cut into integer-length pieces. `prices[i]` is the selling price of a piece of length `i + 1`; no piece longer than `prices.length` can be sold. Return the maximum total revenue from cutting the whole rod (all of it must be used).

title: Best Packing Value
description: Item `i` has weight `weights[i]` and value `values[i]`. A bag holds total weight at most `capacity`. Choose each item at most once. Return the maximum total value that fits.

title: Pick Values With Neighbours Banned
description: In one move you pick a value `x` that is still in `nums`, earn `x` points for every copy of `x`, and then all copies of `x - 1` and `x + 1` are removed. Return the maximum number of points you can earn.

examples.explanation: The maximum number of points is 6.
The maximum number of points is 9.

title: Heaviest Rising Subsequence
description: Among all strictly increasing subsequences of `nums`, return the largest possible sum of their elements.

examples.explanation: The heaviest rising subsequence sums to 25.
The heaviest rising subsequence sums to 5.

title: Longest Arithmetic Subsequence Length
description: Return the length of the longest subsequence of `nums` in which consecutive elements differ by the same constant (the constant may be negative or zero). Any two elements form such a subsequence.

examples.explanation: The longest arithmetic subsequence has length 4.
The longest arithmetic subsequence has length 3.

title: Largest Binary Word Subset
description: `s` is a list of binary words separated by single spaces. Choose a subset of the words (each at most once) that uses at most `m` zeros and at most `n` ones in total. Return the largest possible size of such a subset.
constraints: 1 <= number of words <= 200, 1 <= word length <= 100, only '0' and '1'

title: Smallest Final Stone Weight
description: Repeatedly choose any two stones of weights `x <= y` and smash them: if `x == y` both vanish, otherwise a stone of weight `y - x` remains. Return the smallest possible weight of the last stone, or `0` if no stone is left.

examples.explanation: The smallest possible final weight is 1.
The smallest possible final weight is 5.

title: Fewest Limited Coins
description: You have `counts[i]` coins of value `coins[i]`. Return the minimum number of coins whose values add up to exactly `amount`, or `-1` if that is impossible.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of coins is 5 (-1 means impossible).
The minimum number of coins is -1 (-1 means impossible).

title: Rising Subsequence Count
description: Count the non-empty strictly increasing subsequences of `nums`. Subsequences made of different index sets are different even if their values are equal. Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Largest Sum Divisible By Three
description: Return the largest possible sum of a subset of the elements of `nums` (possibly empty) that is divisible by `3`.

examples.explanation: The largest sum divisible by 3 is 18.
The largest sum divisible by 3 is 0.

title: Count Of Square Submatrices
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table of `0` and `1` stored row by row. Return the number of square submatrices (of any size) that contain only `1`.

title: Binary Search Tree Shapes Count
description: Return the number of structurally different binary search trees that store exactly the keys `1..n` (each key once).
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer

title: Cheapest Frog Path
description: A frog starts on stone `0` of a row of stones with heights `heights`. From stone `i` it can jump to any stone `j` with `i < j <= i + k`, paying `|heights[i] - heights[j]|`. Return the minimum total cost to reach the last stone.

title: Dice Roll Ways
description: Roll `n` dice, each with faces `1..f`. Return the number of ordered outcomes whose faces add up to exactly `target`, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: There are 6 ways to reach the target.
There are 1 ways to reach the target.

title: Phone Pad Knight Paths
description: A chess knight stands on a phone keypad (rows `1 2 3`, `4 5 6`, `7 8 9`, and `0` alone in the middle of the bottom row) and may start on any digit. It makes `n - 1` knight moves, and the digits it lands on form a dialled number of `n` digits. Return the number of distinct `n`-digit numbers it can dial, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: The knight can dial 10 different numbers.
The knight can dial 20 different numbers.

constraints: moves must be legal knight moves between digit keys

title: Longest Shared Substring Length
description: Return the length of the longest contiguous substring that occurs in both `a` and `b` (`0` if they share no letter).

examples.explanation: The longest shared substring has length 4.
The longest shared substring has length 0.

constraints: a and b have lowercase letters only

title: Best Score Difference Taking Ends
description: Two players alternate turns, the first player starting. On each turn a player takes either the first or the last pile of `piles` and adds its stones to their score. Both maximise their own final score. Return the first player's score minus the second player's score.

examples.explanation: The first player wins by 1 (negative means loses).
The first player wins by 7 (negative means loses).

title: Fewest Copy Paste Operations
description: A text editor holds one character `A`. In one operation you may copy everything on screen, or paste the last copied text (appending it). Return the minimum number of operations needed to have exactly `n` copies of `A` on screen.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of operations is 3.
The minimum number of operations is 0.

constraints: copy always copies the whole screen

title: Broken Stairs Ways
description: You climb a staircase of `n` steps (numbered `1..n`), starting on the ground (step `0`) and moving `1` or `2` steps at a time. The steps listed in `broken` cannot be stepped on. Return the number of ways to reach step `n`, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

examples.explanation: There are 2 ways to reach the top.
There are 5 ways to reach the top.

title: Good String Build Count
description: Start with an empty string. In one step you append either `zero` copies of `0` or `one` copies of `1`. A string built this way is good if its length is between `low` and `high` inclusive. Return the number of different good strings, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Longest Running Time Computers
description: You have `n` computers and the batteries in `batteries` (`batteries[i]` is how many minutes battery `i` can power a computer). Each computer needs one battery at a time, and you may swap batteries between computers at any moment for free (a battery can be moved but each minute of charge is used once). Return the largest number of whole minutes during which all `n` computers can run simultaneously.

examples.explanation: All computers can run for 4 minute(s).
All computers can run for 2 minute(s).

title: Fewest Days To Eat Oranges
description: There are `n` oranges. Each day you do exactly one of: eat one orange; if the number left is divisible by `2`, eat half of them; if it is divisible by `3`, eat two thirds of them. Return the minimum number of days to eat all the oranges.
constraints: each day exactly one option is used

title: Single CPU Finish Time
description: `tasks` holds pairs `[enqueue0, process0, enqueue1, process1, ...]`: task `i` becomes available at time `enqueue` and needs `process` time units. A single CPU, when idle, starts the available task with the shortest processing time (ties: the smaller task index); if none is available it waits for the next one. A task runs without interruption. Return the time at which the last task finishes.

examples.explanation: The last task finishes at time 10.
The last task finishes at time 40.

title: Fewest Removals For Half
description: You choose a set of distinct values and delete every occurrence of each chosen value from `nums`. Return the minimum number of distinct values you must choose so that at least half of the elements of `nums` are deleted.

examples.explanation: At least 2 value(s) must be removed.
At least 1 value(s) must be removed.

title: Product After K Increments
description: In one operation you add `1` to any element of `nums`. Perform exactly `k` operations so that the product of all elements is as large as possible. Return that maximum product modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Cheapest Hiring From Both Ends
description: `costs[i]` is the cost to hire worker `i`. You hire exactly `k` workers over `k` rounds. In each round look at the first `candidates` and the last `candidates` workers still unhired (if fewer than `2 * candidates` remain, all of them are candidates) and hire the cheapest one, breaking ties by the smaller index. Return the total cost.

title: Smallest K Pair Sums Total
description: `a` and `b` are sorted in ascending order. Consider the sums `a[i] + b[j]` over all pairs of indices (each pair counted separately, equal sums counted separately too). Return the total of the `k` smallest such sums.

examples.explanation: The k smallest pair sums total 15.
The k smallest pair sums total 4.

constraints: -10^9 <= a[i], b[i] <= 10^9, both sorted, 1 <= k <= min(10^4, a.length * b.length)

title: Closest K Values Sum
description: `nums` is sorted in ascending order. Pick the `k` elements closest to the value `x` (an element `a` is closer than `b` if `|a - x| < |b - x|`, or the distances tie and `a < b`). Return the sum of the `k` chosen elements.

examples.explanation: The k closest values add up to 10.
The k closest values add up to 7.

title: Largest Multiple Of Three
description: Using some or all of the digits in `digits` (each digit at most once, in any order), form the largest possible number that is a multiple of `3`. Return it as a string without leading zeros (a result consisting only of zeros is returned as `"0"`), or an empty string if no multiple of three can be formed.

examples.explanation: The largest multiple of three is "981" (empty means none).
The largest multiple of three is "8760" (empty means none).

title: Reach Zero By Jumping
description: You start at index `start` of `arr`. From index `i` you may jump to `i + arr[i]` or to `i - arr[i]` (jumps outside the array are not allowed). Return `true` if you can reach any index whose value is `0`.

title: Largest Equal Candy Pile
description: `piles[i]` candies are in pile `i`. You may split each pile into any number of smaller piles (but never merge piles). Give each of `k` children one pile, all of the same size `s` (extra piles may stay unused). Return the largest possible `s`, or `0` if it is impossible to give every child at least one candy.

title: Largest Number With Non-Decreasing Digits
description: Return the largest integer that is less than or equal to `n` and whose decimal digits never decrease from left to right.
constraints: the digits of the answer are in non-decreasing order

title: Equal Sum Groups Possible
description: Return `true` if the elements of `nums` can be split into exactly `k` non-empty groups (each element in exactly one group) such that all groups have the same sum.

title: Smallest Unreachable Sum
description: Return the smallest positive integer that cannot be written as the sum of some subset of `nums` (each element used at most once).

title: Merges To Make Array Palindrome
description: In one operation you replace two adjacent elements of `nums` by their sum. Return the minimum number of operations that turn `nums` into a palindrome (an array that reads the same forwards and backwards).

examples.explanation: The minimum number of merges is 2.
The minimum number of merges is 3.

title: Bags Filled With Extra Rocks
description: Bag `i` can hold `capacity[i]` rocks and already holds `rocks[i]`. You have `additionalRocks` more rocks to distribute (any number to any bag, never above capacity). Return the maximum number of bags that can be full.

examples.explanation: At most 3 bag(s) can be filled.
At most 3 bag(s) can be filled.

title: Fewest Sticks To Cover Points
description: Points lie at the positions in `points` on a line. A stick of length `L` placed with its left end at `s` covers every point in `[s, s + L]`. Return the minimum number of sticks needed to cover all points.

title: Fewest Minutes To Repair Cars
description: A mechanic of rank `r` repairs `n` cars in `r * n * n` minutes. All mechanics in `ranks` work at the same time, each on their own share of the `cars` cars. Return the minimum number of minutes needed to repair all cars.

examples.explanation: All cars are repaired after 16 minute(s).
All cars are repaired after 16 minute(s).

title: Paid And Free Painters Cost
description: Wall `i` costs `cost[i]` to paint with a paid painter and takes `time[i]` time units. A free painter paints any wall in exactly `1` time unit at no cost, but can only work while the paid painter is busy. Each wall is painted by one painter, and the paid painter works on one wall at a time. Return the minimum total cost to paint all walls.

title: Best Alternating Subsequence Sum
description: Pick a non-empty subsequence of `nums`. Its alternating sum is `s0 - s1 + s2 - s3 + ...` over its elements in order. Return the maximum alternating sum over all non-empty subsequences.

title: Inventory Sale Maximum Revenue
description: `inventory[i]` is the number of balls of colour `i`. A customer asks for `orders` balls, one at a time. The price of a ball equals the number of balls of its colour currently in stock (so the price drops by one after every sale of that colour). You choose which colour to sell each time. Return the maximum total revenue, modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Mailbox Placement Total Distance
description: Houses stand at the positions in `houses` along a street. Place exactly `k` mailboxes at integer positions (a mailbox may be placed at a house; two mailboxes may not share a position unless there are fewer distinct positions than `k`). Each house walks to its nearest mailbox. Return the minimum possible total walking distance of all houses.

examples.explanation: The minimum total walking distance is 5.
The minimum total walking distance is 9.

title: Smallest Deviation After Doubling Halving
description: In one operation you either divide an even element of `nums` by `2`, or multiply an odd element by `2`. You may repeat operations on any elements any number of times. The deviation of an array is `max - min`. Return the minimum deviation achievable.

title: Most Apples Eaten
description: On day `i` a tree gives `apples[i]` apples that rot after `days[i]` days (they can be eaten on days `i .. i + days[i] - 1`). The tree gives nothing on later days unless listed. You eat at most one apple per day, starting from day `0`, and may keep eating after the last listed day. Return the maximum number of apples you can eat.
constraints: 0 <= apples[i], days[i] <= 2 * 10^4, apples[i] = 0 exactly when days[i] = 0

title: Kth Smallest Product Of Sorted Arrays
description: `a` and `b` are sorted in ascending order and may contain negative numbers and zeros. Consider the products `a[i] * b[j]` over all pairs of indices. Return the `k`-th smallest product (1-indexed, equal products counted separately).
constraints: -10^5 <= a[i], b[j] <= 10^5, both sorted, 1 <= k <= a.length * b.length

title: Fastest Race Completion Time
description: `tires` holds pairs `[f0, r0, f1, r1, ...]`: with tire `i`, the first lap on it takes `f` seconds and each following consecutive lap on the same tire takes `r` times longer than the previous one. A race has `numLaps` laps; after any lap you may change to any tire (including a fresh copy of the same one) for `changeTime` seconds, and there is an unlimited supply of each tire. Return the minimum total time to finish the race, starting on a fresh tire of your choice.

title: Split Stones Score Game
description: A row of stones has values `stones`. In each round Alice splits the current row into two non-empty parts (left and right). Bob discards the part with the larger sum; if both sums are equal Alice chooses which part to discard. Alice's score grows by the sum of the part that remains. The game ends when one stone is left. Return the maximum score Alice can reach.

title: Most Courses Finished In Time
description: `courses` holds pairs `[duration0, lastDay0, duration1, lastDay1, ...]`. Course `i` takes `duration` consecutive days, must be finished on or before `lastDay`, and you attend one course at a time starting on day `1`. Return the maximum number of courses you can finish.

examples.explanation: At most 3 course(s) can be finished.
At most 1 course(s) can be finished.

title: Domino And Tromino Tilings Count
description: A `2 x n` board is tiled without gaps or overlaps using `2 x 1` dominoes (in either orientation) and L-shaped trominoes (three cells, in any of the four rotations). Return the number of different tilings, modulo `10^9 + 7`. Two tilings differ if some pair of cells is covered by one tile in one tiling and by different tiles in the other.

title: Three Colour Grid Paint Ways
description: Paint every cell of an `n x 3` grid red, yellow or green so that no two cells sharing a side have the same colour. Return the number of valid paintings, modulo `10^9 + 7`.
constraints: adjacent cells (sharing an edge) must differ

title: Cheapest Non-Aligned Falling Path
description: `grid` is an `R x C` table stored row by row. Pick exactly one cell in every row so that cells chosen in consecutive rows are in different columns. Return the minimum possible sum of the picked values.
constraints: 1 <= R <= 200, 2 <= C <= 200, grid.length = R * C (C may be 1 only when R = 1)

title: Smallest Difference Between Two Halves
description: `nums` has `2 * n` integers. Split it into two arrays of exactly `n` elements each (every element goes to exactly one array). Return the minimum possible absolute difference between the sums of the two arrays.

title: Most Coins From K Pile Tops
description: Several piles of coins stand side by side. `coins` lists all coin values pile after pile, top coin first, and `sizes[i]` is the number of coins in pile `i`. In one move you take the top coin of any pile. Return the maximum total value of exactly `k` coins you can take.

examples.explanation: The best total value of k coins is 101.
The best total value of k coins is 101.

title: Partitions With Both Sums At Least K
description: Split the elements of `nums` into two groups (every element goes to exactly one group; an ordered pair of groups, so swapping the groups gives a different partition). A partition is great if both group sums are at least `k`. Return the number of great partitions, modulo `10^9 + 7`; partitions that put different index sets in the groups are different even if the values match.

title: Best Gcd Pair Scoring
description: `nums` has `2 * n` positive integers. You perform `n` operations numbered `1..n`. In operation `i` you choose two elements `x` and `y` that have not been used, remove them, and gain `i * gcd(x, y)`. Return the maximum total score.

title: Target Array From Running Sums
description: Start with an array of `n` ones. In one step compute `x`, the sum of all current elements, and replace any single element by `x`. Return `true` if the array `target` can be reached.

title: Obstacle Course Length Total
description: `obstacles[i]` is the height of the `i`-th obstacle. For each index `i`, find the length of the longest non-decreasing subsequence of `obstacles[0..i]` that ends with `obstacles[i]` (the longest course you can take that ends at obstacle `i`). Return the sum of these lengths over all `i`.

examples.explanation: The course lengths add up to 6.
The course lengths add up to 6.

title: Ways To Form Target From Columns
description: `words` is a list of lowercase words of equal length separated by single spaces. You build `target` letter by letter from left to right: to place the `i`-th letter you choose a column `c` and any word whose letter in column `c` equals it; after using column `c`, only columns to its right may be used for the following letters (a column may be left unused, and several words may share a column but only one letter is taken from it). Return the number of ways, modulo `10^9 + 7`. Ways differ if the chosen column or word index differs at some position.

examples.explanation: There are 6 ways to build the target.
There are 4 ways to build the target.

constraints: 1 <= number of words <= 1000, 1 <= word length <= 1000, all words have equal length

title: Fewest Trips Delivering Boxes
description: `boxes` holds pairs `[port0, weight0, port1, weight1, ...]` for boxes that must be delivered in the given order from a storage depot. A truck carries a batch of consecutive boxes (at most `maxBoxes` boxes and total weight at most `maxWeight`), visits their ports in order (it stops once at a port if neighbouring boxes of the batch share it, and once per change otherwise), then returns to the depot. A trip is one leg: depot to the first port, each move to a different port, and the return. Return the minimum total number of trips (legs) to deliver all boxes.

examples.explanation: The minimum number of trips is 4.
The minimum number of trips is 6.

title: Fewest Minutes To Build Blocks
description: You must build every block; block `i` takes `blocks[i]` minutes for one worker to build. You start with one worker. In one step a worker either builds one block (and is then finished) or splits into two workers, which takes `split` minutes; workers act in parallel. Return the minimum number of minutes until all blocks are built.

examples.explanation: All blocks are built after 4 minute(s).
All blocks are built after 7 minute(s).

title: Arrays With Exactly K Records
description: Count the arrays of length `n` whose elements are integers from `1` to `m` and in which exactly `k` elements are strict prefix records (an element is a record if it is larger than every element before it; the first element is always a record). Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Non-Overlapping Segment Sets Count
description: `n` points stand on a line at positions `0, 1, ..., n - 1`. A segment covers at least two points: it runs from one point to a later point. Count the ways to draw exactly `k` segments that do not overlap (two segments may share an end point but may not cover a common stretch of length greater than zero). Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`; ways are different if the set of segments differs.

title: Fewest Incompatibility Groups
description: Divide `nums` into `k` groups of equal size so that no group contains two equal values. The incompatibility of a group is its maximum minus its minimum, and the cost of a division is the sum of the group incompatibilities. Return the minimum cost, or `-1` if no valid division exists. `nums.length` is divisible by `k`.

examples.explanation: The minimum total incompatibility is 4 (-1 means impossible).
The minimum total incompatibility is 6 (-1 means impossible).

constraints: 1 <= k <= nums.length <= 16, nums.length is divisible by k

title: Students Seating Without Cheating
description: A classroom is an `R x C` grid stored row by row; `grid[i*C+j]` is `1` for a usable seat and `0` for a broken one. A student can see the answers of the students to their left, right, upper-left and upper-right (not directly ahead). Place students on usable seats so that nobody can see another student's paper, and return the maximum number of students that can sit for the exam.

title: Cheapest Two-Group Connection
description: There are two groups of points with `n1` points in the first group and `n2` points in the second (`n1 >= n2`). `cost` is an `n1 x n2` table stored row by row; `cost[i*n2+j]` is the price to connect point `i` of the first group with point `j` of the second. The groups are connected if every point of each group is joined to at least one point of the other group. Return the minimum total cost of the chosen connections.
